items.title: Cosimo Matassa Interview, 1993-05-28

ctx.x: He was Joseph DiGuardi. D-I-G-U-A-R-D-I. And, yeah. And I came up hearing Mazurkas and Polkas and Schottisches and Marches. Mm-hmm. I mean, Under the Double Eagle was a staple. Mm-hmm. And things like that. And, of course, I also heard them because in those days, the jazz bands on the street played them a lot more than they do now. And for some reason, those original things aren't played as much. When you go to a place now and listen to Dixieland or traditional jazz, you don't hear as many of those kinds of…
When would you hear the family play? When would you hear your relatives play?
